expectations.text: Writes the LDAP fix in symptom phrasing an administrator can match to a support ticket
expectations.evidence: §4 leaves the actual LDAP description as a placeholder: "**What changes:** {{Precise before/after. Example shape only — replace with the real behaviour...}}", so the shipped entry contains no real symptom an admin could match. The illustrative example does gesture at observable behaviour ("sync run aborts, last-known-good membership is retained... instead of failing open (sync proceeds with an empty group set)") and the required-action example is the strongest moment — "a sync that previously failed open and went unnoticed will now block role updates and surface as a support ticket" — explicit

expectations.text: Writes the LDAP fix in symptom phrasing an administrator can match to a support ticket
expectations.evidence: CHG-2 is framed entirely in mechanism terms, not observable symptoms. The summary placeholder instructs '[One sentence naming the mechanism, e.g. "Ridgeway's LDAP sync now resolves nested group membership; it previously evaluated only direct membership."]' and the previous-behavior field asks the author to 'Describe precisely: which attribute/query was used, what was and wasn't evaluated' — both push toward internal-implementation phrasing rather than 'users in nested groups were silently denied access they should have had.'
